asr_bad_lines: So let's put these home tests on trial, only ones worth your time.
The fakes built from cheaper fats, like palm oil and vanispati.
Last month in Junegar police say they found soybean oil in bottles of essence, in tins sold as pure cow ghee.
Test 2 your palm, your hands warm so ghee melts.
Test 4 color, yellows good whites bad.
The acid tests on the official list. It turns crimson if there's vanispatty.
But milk fat has a tiny fat palm oil doesn't, called butyric acid. About 2.5% in ghee, 0 in palm oil.
A lab can count it and catch palm oil down to about 5%. Your hand can't count.
Look for the license number, the maker, a batch number and an expiry date. Those Junigar tins had no batch number and no expiry.
